content: Do not overlook the humble violet beneath your feet while gazing at distant summits.
author: Japanese Proverbs
explanation: We spend decades fixated on distant mountain peaks—the future promotion, the retirement cottage, the ideal relationship—while trampling over the fragile, fragrant wildflowers blooming along the gravel beneath our boots. Paradise is not a destination; it is attention.
practicalInsight: Look around you right now. Find one small, ordinary object or person and spend thirty seconds genuinely appreciating their existence.
reflectionPrompt: What simple daily blessing have you been ignoring because your gaze is chronically locked onto distant horizons?
